ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit in the attached figure has a bottom common wire, which can be taken as the reference ground. Between the upper left node and the upper right node there is a resistor labeled 2Ω, and the arrow of current I goes from left to right along this upper resistor. The upper left node is also connected to a vertical 2Ω resistor to the lower common node; the far-left branch is a 6V voltage source with the upper terminal positive and the lower terminal negative in series with a 2Ω resistor connected to the bottom. The upper right node is connected to a 6A current source to the lower common node, with the current source arrow upward; on the right side there is also a vertical 2Ω resistor connected to the bottom common node. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the bottom node as ground, and let the upper left node voltage be V_A and the upper right node voltage be V_B. At node A, write KCL according to currents leaving node A: the current through the vertical 2Ω resistor is V_A/2; the current through the left branch containing the 6V source and the 2Ω resistor is (V_A-6)/2; the current flowing to B through the upper 2Ω resistor is (V_A-V_B)/2. Therefore V_A/2+(V_A-6)/2+(V_A-V_B)/2=0, simplifying gives 3V_A-V_B=6. At node B, the currents leaving the node through the right 2Ω resistor and the upper 2Ω resistor are provided by the injection of the upward 6A current source, so V_B/2+(V_B-V_A)/2=6, simplifying gives -V_A+2V_B=12. Solving 3V_A-V_B=6 together with -V_A+2V_B=12 gives V_A=4.8V, V_B=8.4V. According to the reference direction of I in the figure from left to right, I=(V_A-V_B)/2=(4.8-8.4)/2=-1.8A.
